note: Attacker-controlled PNG bytes are first parsed as image metadata, establishing that the same input will later be decoded.
The header scan walks PNG chunks and records image properties without fully decoding pixels.
A 16-bit grayscale PNG with a tRNS chunk sets up transparency processing for a 16-bit output path.
The same crafted PNG is then fully loaded, reusing the parsed transparency metadata during decode.
When the decoder expands the 16-bit grayscale pixel data, it applies color-key transparency to the output buffer.
The sink reads and writes 16-bit pixel components in the output buffer; the crafted image drives this path and triggers the MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value in the transparency computation.
